2|*****
3|Pajek
4|*****
5|Read graphs in Pajek format.
6|
7|This implementation handles directed and undirected graphs including
8|those with self loops and parallel edges.  
9|
10|Format
11|------
12|
13|See http://vlado.fmf.uni-lj.si/pub/networks/pajek/doc/draweps.htm
14|for format information.
15|"""
16|__author__ = """Aric Hagberg (hagberg@lanl.gov)"""
17|#    Copyright (C) 2008-2010 by 
18|#    Aric Hagberg <hagberg@lanl.gov>
19|#    Dan Schult <dschult@colgate.edu>
20|#    Pieter Swart <swart@lanl.gov>
21|#    All rights reserved.
22|#    BSD license.
23|import networkx as nx
24|from networkx.utils import is_string_like,get_file_handle,make_str
25|
26|__all__ = ['read_pajek', 'parse_pajek', 'generate_pajek', 'write_pajek']

28|def generate_pajek(G):
29|    """Generate lines in Pajek graph format.
30|
31|    Parameters
32|    ----------
33|    G : graph
34|       A Networkx graph
35|
36|    References
37|    ----------
38|    See http://vlado.fmf.uni-lj.si/pub/networks/pajek/doc/draweps.htm
39|    for format information.
40|    """
41|    if G.name=='': 
42|        name='NetworkX'
43|    else:
44|        name=G.name
45|    yield '*network %s'%name
46|
47|    # write nodes with attributes
48|    yield '*vertices %s'%(G.order())
49|    nodes = G.nodes()
50|    # make dictionary mapping nodes to integers
51|    nodenumber=dict(zip(nodes,range(1,len(nodes)+1))) 
52|    for n in nodes:
53|        na=G.node.get(n,{})
54|        x=na.get('x',0.0)
55|        y=na.get('y',0.0)
56|        id=int(na.get('id',nodenumber[n]))
57|        nodenumber[n]=id
58|        shape=na.get('shape','ellipse')
59|        s=' '.join(map(make_str,(id,n,x,y,shape)))
60|        for k,v in na.items():
61|            if is_string_like(v):
62|                # add quotes to any values with a blank space
63|                if " " in v: 
64|                    v="\"%s\""%v
65|            s+=' %s %s'%(k,v)
66|        yield s
67|
68|    # write edges with attributes         
69|    if G.is_directed():
70|        yield '*arcs'
71|    else:
72|        yield '*edges'
73|    for u,v,edgedata in G.edges(data=True):
74|        d=edgedata.copy()
75|        value=d.pop('weight',1.0) # use 1 as default edge value
76|        s=' '.join(map(make_str,(nodenumber[u],nodenumber[v],value)))
77|        for k,v in d.items():
78|            if is_string_like(v):
79|                # add quotes to any values with a blank space
80|                if " " in v: 
81|                    v="\"%s\""%v
82|            s+=' %s %s'%(k,v)
83|        yield s
84|        
85|def write_pajek(G, path, encoding='UTF-8'):
86|    """Write graph in Pajek format to path.
87|
88|    Parameters
89|    ----------
90|    G : graph
91|       A Networkx graph
92|    path : file or string
93|       File or filename to write.  
94|       Filenames ending in .gz or .bz2 will be compressed.
95|
96|    Examples
97|    --------
98|    >>> G=nx.path_graph(4)
99|    >>> nx.write_pajek(G, "test.net")
100|
101|    References
102|    ----------
103|    See http://vlado.fmf.uni-lj.si/pub/networks/pajek/doc/draweps.htm
104|    for format information.
105|    """
106|    fh=get_file_handle(path, 'wb')
107|    for line in generate_pajek(G):
108|        line+='\n'
109|        fh.write(line.encode(encoding))

111|def read_pajek(path,encoding='UTF-8'):
112|    """Read graph in Pajek format from path. 
113|
114|    Parameters
115|    ----------
116|    path : file or string
117|       File or filename to write.  
118|       Filenames ending in .gz or .bz2 will be uncompressed.
119|
120|    Returns
121|    -------
122|    G : NetworkX MultiGraph or MultiDiGraph.
123|
124|    Examples
125|    --------
126|    >>> G=nx.path_graph(4)
127|    >>> nx.write_pajek(G, "test.net")
128|    >>> G=nx.read_pajek("test.net")
129|
130|    To create a Graph instead of a MultiGraph use
131|
132|    >>> G1=nx.Graph(G)
133|
134|    References
135|    ----------
136|    See http://vlado.fmf.uni-lj.si/pub/networks/pajek/doc/draweps.htm
137|    for format information.
138|    """
139|    fh=get_file_handle(path, 'rb')
140|    lines = (line.decode(encoding) for line in fh)
141|    return parse_pajek(lines)
142|
143|def parse_pajek(lines):
144|    """Parse Pajek format graph from string or iterable.
145|
146|    Parameters
147|    ----------
148|    lines : string or iterable
149|       Data in Pajek format.
150|
151|    Returns
152|    -------
153|    G : NetworkX graph
154|
155|    See Also
156|    --------
157|    read_pajek()
158|
159|    """
160|    import shlex
161|    # multigraph=False
162|    if is_string_like(lines): lines=iter(lines.split('\n'))
163|    lines = iter([line.rstrip('\n') for line in lines])
164|    G=nx.MultiDiGraph() # are multiedges allowed in Pajek? assume yes
165|    while lines:
166|        try:
167|            l=next(lines)
168|        except: #EOF
169|            break
170|        if l.lower().startswith("*network"):
171|            label,name=l.split()
172|            G.name=name
173|        if l.lower().startswith("*vertices"):
174|            nodelabels={}
175|            l,nnodes=l.split()
176|            for i in range(int(nnodes)):
177|                splitline=shlex.split(str(next(lines)))
178|                id,label=splitline[0:2]
179|                G.add_node(label)
180|                nodelabels[id]=label
181|                G.node[label]={'id':id}
182|                try: 
183|                    x,y,shape=splitline[2:5]
184|                    G.node[label].update({'x':float(x),
185|                                          'y':float(y),
186|                                          'shape':shape})
187|                except:
188|                    pass
189|                extra_attr=zip(splitline[5::2],splitline[6::2])
190|                G.node[label].update(extra_attr)
191|        if l.lower().startswith("*edges") or l.lower().startswith("*arcs"):
192|            if l.lower().startswith("*edge"):
193|               # switch from multidigraph to multigraph
194|                G=nx.MultiGraph(G)
195|            if l.lower().startswith("*arcs"):
196|               # switch to directed with multiple arcs for each existing edge
197|                G=G.to_directed()
198|            for l in lines:
199|                splitline=shlex.split(str(l))
200|                if len(splitline)<2:
201|                    continue
202|                ui,vi=splitline[0:2]
203|                u=nodelabels.get(ui,ui)
204|                v=nodelabels.get(vi,vi)
205|                # parse the data attached to this edge and put in a dictionary 
206|                edge_data={}
207|                try:
208|                    # there should always be a single value on the edge?
209|                    w=splitline[2:3]
210|                    edge_data.update({'weight':float(w[0])})
211|                except:
212|                    pass
213|                    # if there isn't, just assign a 1
214|#                    edge_data.update({'value':1})
215|                extra_attr=zip(splitline[3::2],splitline[4::2])
216|                edge_data.update(extra_attr)
217|                # if G.has_edge(u,v):
218|                #     multigraph=True
219|                G.add_edge(u,v,**edge_data)
220|    return G
221|
222|
223|# fixture for nose tests
224|def teardown_module(module):
225|    import os
226|    os.unlink('test.net')

362|
363|    Each unionFind instance X maintains a family of disjoint sets of
364|    hashable objects, supporting the following two methods:
365|
366|    - X[item] returns a name for the set containing the given item.
367|      Each set is named by an arbitrarily-chosen one of its members; as
368|      long as the set remains unchanged it will keep the same name. If
369|      the item is not yet part of a set in X, a new singleton set is
370|      created for it.
371|
372|    - X.union(item1, item2, ...) merges the sets containing each item
373|      into a single larger set.  If any item is not yet part of a set
374|      in X, it is added to X as one of the members of the merged set.
375|
376|      Union-find data structure. Based on Josiah Carlson's code,
377|      http://aspn.activestate.com/ASPN/Cookbook/Python/Recipe/215912
378|      with significant additional changes by D. Eppstein.
379|      http://www.ics.uci.edu/~eppstein/PADS/UnionFind.py
380|

384|        """Create a new empty union-find structure."""
385|        self.weights = {}
386|        self.parents = {}
387|

390|
391|        # check for previously unknown object
392|        if object not in self.parents:
393|            self.parents[object] = object
394|            self.weights[object] = 1
395|            return object
396|

398|        path = [object]

400|        while root != path[-1]:
401|            path.append(root)
402|            root = self.parents[root]
403|
404|        # compress the path and return
405|        for ancestor in path:
406|            self.parents[ancestor] = root
407|        return root

411|        return iter(self.parents)

267|    strings.  For example, a list as edge data

269|    as::

272|         source 1
273|         target 2

275|       ]

278|    dicttype=type({})
279|    def listify(d,indent,indentlevel):
280|        result='[ \n'
281|        dicttype=type({})
282|        for k,v in d.items():
283|            if type(v)==dicttype:
284|                v=listify(v,indent,indentlevel+1)
285|            result += indentlevel*indent+"%s %s\n"%(k,v)
286|        return result+indentlevel*indent+"]"

291|    else:

295|    else:

89|def parse_gml(lines, relabel=True):
90|    """Parse GML graph from a string or iterable.
91|
92|    Parameters
93|    ----------
94|    lines : string or iterable
95|       Data in GML format.
96|
97|    relabel : bool, optional       
98|       If True use the GML node label attribute for node names otherwise use
99|       the node id.
100|
101|    Returns
102|    -------
103|    G : MultiGraph or MultiDiGraph
104|
105|    Raises
106|    ------
107|    ImportError
108|        If the pyparsing module is not available.
109|
110|    See Also
111|    --------
112|    write_gml, read_gml
113|    
114|    Notes
115|    -----
116|    This stores nested GML attributes as dictionaries in the 
117|    NetworkX graph, node, and edge attribute structures.
118|
119|    Requires pyparsing: http://pyparsing.wikispaces.com/
120|
121|    References
122|    ----------
123|    GML specification:
124|    http://www.infosun.fim.uni-passau.de/Graphlet/GML/gml-tr.html
125|    """
126|    try:
127|        from pyparsing import ParseException
128|    except ImportError:
129|        try:
130|            from matplotlib.pyparsing import ParseException
131|        except:
132|            raise ImportError('Import Error: not able to import pyparsing:', 
133|                              'http://pyparsing.wikispaces.com/')

135|        data = "".join(lines)
136|        gml = pyparse_gml()
137|        tokens =gml.parseString(data)
138|    except ParseException as err:
139|        print((err.line))
140|        print((" "*(err.column-1) + "^"))
141|        print(err)
142|        raise
143|
144|    # function to recursively make dicts of key/value pairs
145|    def wrap(tok):
146|        listtype=type(tok)
147|        result={}
148|        for k,v in tok:
149|            if type(v)==listtype:
150|                result[str(k)]=wrap(v)
151|            else:
152|                result[str(k)]=v
153|        return result
154|
155|    # Set flag
156|    multigraph=False
157|    # but assume multigraphs to start
158|    if tokens.directed==1:
159|        G=nx.MultiDiGraph()
160|    else:
161|        G=nx.MultiGraph()
162|
163|    for k,v in tokens.asList():
164|        if k=="node":
165|            vdict=wrap(v)
166|            node=vdict['id']
167|            G.add_node(node,attr_dict=vdict)
168|        elif k=="edge":
169|            vdict=wrap(v)
170|            source=vdict.pop('source')
171|            target=vdict.pop('target')
172|            if G.has_edge(source,target):
173|                multigraph=True
174|            G.add_edge(source,target,attr_dict=vdict)
175|        else:
176|            G.graph[k]=v
177|
178|    # switch to Graph or DiGraph if no parallel edges were found.
179|    if not multigraph: 
180|        if G.is_directed():
181|            G=nx.DiGraph(G)
182|        else:
183|            G=nx.Graph(G)
184|
185|    if relabel:
186|        # relabel, but check for duplicate labels first
187|        mapping=[(n,d['label']) for n,d in G.node.items()]
188|        x,y=zip(*mapping)

190|            raise NetworkXError('Failed to relabel nodes: '
191|                                'duplicate node labels found. '
192|                                'Use relabel=False.')
193|        G=nx.relabel_nodes(G,dict(mapping))

197|def pyparse_gml():
198|    """A pyparsing tokenizer for GML graph format.
199|
200|    This is not intended to be called directly.
201|
202|    See Also
203|    --------
204|    write_gml, read_gml, parse_gml
205|    """  
206|    try:
207|        from pyparsing import \
208|             Literal, CaselessLiteral, Word, Forward,\
209|             ZeroOrMore, Group, Dict, Optional, Combine,\
210|             ParseException, restOfLine, White, alphas, alphanums, nums,\
211|             OneOrMore,quotedString,removeQuotes,dblQuotedString, Regex
212|    except ImportError:
213|        try:
214|            from matplotlib.pyparsing import \
215|             Literal, CaselessLiteral, Word, Forward,\
216|             ZeroOrMore, Group, Dict, Optional, Combine,\
217|             ParseException, restOfLine, White, alphas, alphanums, nums,\
218|             OneOrMore,quotedString,removeQuotes,dblQuotedString, Regex
219|        except:
220|            raise ImportError('pyparsing not found',
221|                              'http://pyparsing.wikispaces.com/')
222|
223|    lbrack = Literal("[").suppress()
224|    rbrack = Literal("]").suppress()
225|    pound = ("#")
226|    comment = pound + Optional( restOfLine )
227|    integer = Word(nums+'-').setParseAction(lambda s,l,t:[ int(t[0])])
228|    real = Regex(r"[+-]?\d+\.\d*([eE][+-]?\d+)?").setParseAction(
229|        lambda s,l,t:[ float(t[0]) ])
230|    dblQuotedString.setParseAction( removeQuotes )
231|    key = Word(alphas,alphanums+'_')
232|    value_atom = (real | integer | Word(alphanums) | dblQuotedString) 
233|    value = Forward()   # to be defined later with << operator
234|    keyvalue = Group(key+value)
235|    value << (value_atom | Group( lbrack + ZeroOrMore(keyvalue) + rbrack ))
236|    node = Group(Literal("node") + lbrack + Group(OneOrMore(keyvalue)) + rbrack)
237|    edge = Group(Literal("edge") + lbrack + Group(OneOrMore(keyvalue)) + rbrack)
238|
239|    creator = Group(Literal("Creator")+ Optional( restOfLine ))
240|    version = Group(Literal("Version")+ Optional( restOfLine ))
241|    graphkey = Literal("graph").suppress()
242|
243|    graph = Dict (Optional(creator)+Optional(version)+\
244|        graphkey + lbrack + ZeroOrMore( (node|edge|keyvalue) ) + rbrack )
245|    graph.ignore(comment)
246|    
247|    return graph

249|def generate_gml(G):
250|    """Generate a single entry of the graph G in GML format.
251|
252|    Parameters
253|    ----------
254|    G : NetworkX graph
255|
256|    Returns
257|    -------
258|    lines: string
259|       Lines in GML format.
260|
261|    Notes
262|    -----
263|    This implementation does not support all Python data types as GML
264|    data.  Nodes, node attributes, edge attributes, and graph
265|    attributes must be either dictionaries or single stings or
266|    numbers.  If they are not an attempt is made to represent them as
267|    strings.  For example, a list as edge data
268|    G[1][2]['somedata']=[1,2,3], will be represented in the GML file
269|    as::
270|
271|       edge [
272|         source 1
273|         target 2
274|         somedata "[1, 2, 3]"
275|       ]
276|    """
277|    # recursively make dicts into gml brackets
278|    dicttype=type({})
279|    def listify(d,indent,indentlevel):
280|        result='[ \n'
281|        dicttype=type({})
282|        for k,v in d.items():
283|            if type(v)==dicttype:
284|                v=listify(v,indent,indentlevel+1)
285|            result += indentlevel*indent+"%s %s\n"%(k,v)
286|        return result+indentlevel*indent+"]"
287|
288|    # check for attributes or assign empty dict
289|    if hasattr(G,'graph_attr'):
290|        graph_attr=G.graph_attr
291|    else:
292|        graph_attr={}
293|    if hasattr(G,'node_attr'):
294|        node_attr=G.node_attr
295|    else:
296|        node_attr={}
297|
298|    indent=2*' '
299|    count=iter(range(len(G)))
300|    node_id={}
301|
302|    yield "graph ["
303|    if G.is_directed():
304|        yield indent+"directed 1"
305|    # write graph attributes 
306|    for k,v in G.graph.items():
307|        if type(v)==dicttype: 
308|            v=listify(v,indent,2)
309|        elif is_string_like(v):
310|            v='"%s"'%v
311|        yield indent+"%s %s"%(k,v)
312|    # write nodes
313|    for n in G:
314|        yield indent+"node ["
315|        # get id or assign number
316|        nid=G.node[n].get('id',next(count))
317|        node_id[n]=nid
318|        yield 2*indent+"id %s"%nid
319|        label=G.node[n].pop('label',n)
320|        if is_string_like(label):
321|            label='"%s"'%label
322|        yield 2*indent+'label %s'%label
323|        if n in G:
324|          for k,v in G.node[n].items():
325|              if k=='id': continue
326|              if type(v)==dicttype: 
327|                  v=listify(v,indent,3)
328|              elif is_string_like(v):
329|                  v='"%s"'%v
330|              yield 2*indent+"%s %s"%(k,v)
331|        yield indent+"]"
332|    # write edges
333|    for u,v,edgedata in G.edges_iter(data=True):
334|        # try to guess what is on the edge and do something reasonable
335|        yield indent+"edge ["
336|        yield 2*indent+"source %s"%node_id[u]
337|        yield 2*indent+"target %s"%node_id[v]
338|        for k,v in edgedata.items():
339|            if k=='source': continue
340|            if k=='target': continue
341|            if type(v)==dicttype: 
342|                v=listify(v,indent,3)
343|            elif is_string_like(v):
344|                v='"%s"'%v
345|            yield 2*indent+"%s %s"%(k,v)
346|        yield indent+"]"
347|    yield "]"

351|    """
352|    Write the graph G in GML format to the file or file handle path.
353|
354|    Parameters
355|    ----------
356|    path : filename or filehandle
357|       The filename or filehandle to write.  Filenames ending in
358|       .gz or .gz2 will be compressed.
359|
360|    See Also
361|    --------
362|    read_gml, parse_gml
363|
364|    Notes
365|    -----
366|    GML specifications indicate that the file should only use
367|    7bit ASCII text encoding.iso8859-1 (latin-1). 
368|
369|    This implementation does not support all Python data types as GML
370|    data.  Nodes, node attributes, edge attributes, and graph
371|    attributes must be either dictionaries or single stings or
372|    numbers.  If they are not an attempt is made to represent them as
373|    strings.  For example, a list as edge data
374|    G[1][2]['somedata']=[1,2,3], will be represented in the GML file
375|    as::

378|         source 1
379|         target 2

381|       ]
